key_insight: Bayesian inference on photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion simulations can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade—at the hole/electron transport interfaces or in the bulk.
engineering_relevance: The method helps engineers identify the dominant failure mode in a specific device region, enabling targeted interface passivation and more durable perovskite solar cell designs.
method: Capture photoluminescence images of fully fabricated devices during aging.
Couple imaging with drift-diffusion simulations to infer spatial maps of recombination-related parameters.
Track how inferred maps evolve under 70 °C full-spectrum sunlight to separate degradation mechanisms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports temporally evolving, spatially heterogeneous parameter maps that reveal strongest degradation at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces and improvement after amino-silane passivation.
watch_item: Inference quality depends on the fidelity of the optical model and simulation assumptions, so parameter maps should be validated carefully before making design decisions.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
